accepted.s: The term ‘tsunami’ is derived from which combination of Japanese words and meanings?
accepted.x: In Japanese, ‘tsu’ means harbour and ‘nami’ means wave; hence tsunami literally means ‘harbour wave’.
accepted.tq: Test the exact meaning of a look-alike term rather than accepting the familiar but incorrect ‘tidal wave’.
accepted.sec: Tsunamis - causes, meaning, source ocean, deep-sea vs coast, 2004 event  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a tsunami from a tidal wave?
o: A tsunami results from sudden displacement of the ocean floor, whereas tides result mainly from gravitational pull.
A tsunami consists of a single wave, whereas tides always consist of multiple waves.
A tsunami is confined to shallow water, whereas tides occur only in deep oceans.
A tsunami is caused by gravitational attraction, whereas a tidal wave is caused by earthquakes.
accepted.x: Tsunamis are generated by sudden displacement of the ocean floor, usually due to tectonic activity. Tides are produced mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun.
accepted.tq: Separate two commonly confused terms by matching each with its actual cause.
accepted.sec: Tsunamis - causes, meaning, source ocean, deep-sea vs coast, 2004 event  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the causes of tsunamis:
1. Subduction-related undersea earthquakes are the chief cause of tsunamis.
2. Submarine landslides and volcanic eruptions can also generate tsunamis.
3. Asteroid or meteorite impacts in the ocean can produce tsunamis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Tsunamis may result from tectonic earthquakes, submarine landslides, volcanic eruptions and large asteroid or meteorite impacts.
accepted.tq: Use the inclusive option after checking whether every listed triggering mechanism is supported.
accepted.sec: Tsunamis - causes, meaning, source ocean, deep-sea vs coast, 2004 event  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations regarding tsunami behaviour is correctly matched?
o: Near coast—long wavelength and declining wave height
Deep ocean—long wavelength and low wave height
Deep ocean—short wavelength and very high wave height
Near coast—high speed and barely noticeable waves
accepted.x: In the deep ocean, a tsunami has a very long wavelength, low height and high speed. Its height increases considerably near the coast as it enters shallow water.
accepted.tq: Compare the same phenomenon in two settings and identify the correct paired characteristics.
accepted.sec: Tsunamis - causes, meaning, source ocean, deep-sea vs coast, 2004 event  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A tsunami travelling through the deep ocean may attain a speed of approximately:
accepted.x: Tsunamis can travel at speeds of up to about 800 km/h in the deep ocean, where their height remains relatively low.
accepted.tq: Use the distinct quantitative figure associated with deep-ocean tsunami propagation.
accepted.sec: Tsunamis - causes, meaning, source ocean, deep-sea vs coast, 2004 event  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Why does a tsunami become particularly destructive near the coast?
o: The wave slows in shallow water and its height rises sharply through shoaling.
The wave gains speed because coastal water is deeper.
The wave loses all its energy through evaporation.
The wave changes into a tidal current due to lunar attraction.
accepted.x: As a tsunami enters shallow coastal water, its speed decreases and its wave height rises sharply, producing severe inundation.
accepted.tq: Apply the deep-ocean versus shallow-coast comparison to explain coastal inundation.
accepted.sec: Tsunamis - causes, meaning, source ocean, deep-sea vs coast, 2004 event  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Tsunamis affecting India mostly originate from which combination of regions?
o: Bering Sea and Gulf of Mexico
accepted.x: Most tsunamis affecting India originate in the Indian Ocean, particularly from the Sunda-Andaman subduction zone; the Makran zone poses a threat to India’s west coast.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure geographical source and distinguish the eastern and western Indian Ocean threat zones.
accepted.sec: Tsunamis - causes, meaning, source ocean, deep-sea vs coast, 2004 event  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct order of tsunami risk zones from highest to moderate risk in India?
o: Tamil Nadu—Andaman and Nicobar—Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra and Gujarat
Andhra Pradesh and Odisha—Gujarat and Maharashtra—Andaman and Nicobar
Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra and Gujarat—Tamil Nadu—Andaman and Nicobar
Andaman and Nicobar—Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry and Odisha—Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra and Gujarat
accepted.x: Andaman and Nicobar Islands are in the very-high-risk zone; Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry and Odisha are in the high-risk zone; Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra and Gujarat are in the moderate-risk zone.
accepted.tq: Read the risk classification from highest to moderate without reversing the geographical grouping.
accepted.sec: Tsunamis - causes, meaning, source ocean, deep-sea vs coast, 2004 event  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Indian Ocean tsunami of 26 December 2004, consider the following statements:
1. It was triggered by an earthquake near the Sumatra-Andaman region.
2. The earthquake had a magnitude of approximately 9.1.
3. Nagapattinam was the worst-affected district in Tamil Nadu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 26 December 2004 tsunami was generated by an approximately magnitude 9.1 Sumatra-Andaman earthquake, and Nagapattinam was the worst-affected district in Tamil Nadu.
accepted.tq: Combine event, magnitude and location facts; the all-inclusive option is correct when each detail fits.
accepted.sec: Tsunamis - causes, meaning, source ocean, deep-sea vs coast, 2004 event  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT listed among the Indian regions affected by the tsunami of 26 December 2004?
accepted.x: The affected Indian regions listed were the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Puducherry. Gujarat was not included in that list.
accepted.tq: Find the excluded location by checking the event-specific affected-region list.
accepted.sec: Tsunamis - causes, meaning, source ocean, deep-sea vs coast, 2004 event  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A flood is best defined as a situation in which:
o: Only coastal water enters an urban settlement during a cyclone.
Water exceeds channel capacity and spills over normally dry land.
Groundwater permanently disappears from a drainage basin.
Water remains confined within a river channel after heavy rainfall.
accepted.x: A flood occurs when the volume of water exceeds the carrying capacity of a channel and spills onto land that is normally dry.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise definition rather than selecting a related but narrower coastal or rainfall condition.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a characteristic of an ordinary riverine flood as distinguished from a flash flood?
o: It occurs only after a glacial lake bursts.
It is generally slow-onset and can be regionally and seasonally predictable.
It is caused only by submarine earthquakes.
It develops within minutes exclusively in steep mountain valleys.
accepted.x: Ordinary floods are generally slow-onset and often predictable in terms of region and season, unlike the sudden nature of flash floods.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related hazard types using onset and predictability.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following sets contains only causes of floods identified for India?
1. Heavy or prolonged rainfall
2. Poor drainage and low infiltration
3. Deforestation and dam failure
4. Siltation resulting from soil erosion
accepted.x: Heavy rainfall, poor drainage, low infiltration, deforestation, dam failure and siltation from soil erosion are all recognised causes of floods.
accepted.tq: Check whether each listed causal factor belongs to the same hazard rather than selecting a partial combination.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a cause of flooding included in the given classification?
accepted.x: Snow and ice melt, storm surges and river siltation are listed flood causes. Volcanic ash fertilisation of soil is not a stated cause of flooding.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the unrelated process while retaining causes connected with water accumulation or drainage obstruction.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, riverine flooding is particularly associated with which geographical region?
o: The Pennar headwaters in Karnataka only
accepted.x: The Krishna-Godavari deltaic region is especially associated with riverine flooding in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the location-specific association between a flood type and the vulnerable physical region.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Riverine flooding in the Krishna-Godavari region may become particularly severe when water is released simultaneously from:
accepted.x: Flooding in the Krishna-Godavari region can be especially severe when Srisailam, Nagarjuna Sagar and Hirakud release water together.
accepted.tq: Test the linked dam names through a same-basin and downstream-impact association.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What does the term GLOF refer to?
accepted.x: GLOF stands for Glacial Lake Outburst Flood, a sudden flood caused by the bursting of a glacial or proglacial lake.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of a disaster acronym before applying its mechanism.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly explains the formation of a glacial lake outburst flood?
o: Glacier retreat → enlargement of a proglacial lake → bursting of the lake → flood
Deforestation → oceanic tide → lake freezing → flood
River siltation → volcanic eruption → glacier advance → flood
Rain shadow → soil erosion → sea-level fall → flood
accepted.x: Glacier retreat can enlarge proglacial lakes; when the lake bursts, the stored water produces a glacial lake outburst flood.
accepted.tq: Arrange the causal chain from environmental change to disaster occurrence.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding glacial changes and GLOF-related information is correct?
1. The South Lhonak GLOF occurred in Sikkim in October 2023.
2. The world lost more than 9,500 gigatonnes of glacier mass since 1975.
3. Glacier area in the Central Himalaya declined by more than 20 per cent in three decades.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the South Lhonak GLOF occurred in October 2023, global glacier mass loss exceeded 9,500 Gt since 1975, and Central Himalayan glacier area declined by more than 20 per cent in three decades.
accepted.tq: Cross-check event, global magnitude and regional percentage before choosing the combined code.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The catastrophic flash floods reported in Nepal on 26 August 2026 were associated with which hazard?
o: Tsunami generated in the Indian Ocean
accepted.x: The event was identified as a catastrophic flash-flood episode associated with GLOF-related conditions in Nepal.
accepted.tq: Match the dated event with its specific hydrological-disaster category.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Dharali flash flood of 5 August 2025 in Uttarakhand was attributed to the collapse of an ice patch on which glacier?
accepted.x: An ISRO study attributed the Dharali flash flood to the collapse of an ice patch on the Srikanta Glacier.
accepted.tq: Use the event-location-cause combination and avoid substituting a better-known glacier name.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Approximately how much area was assessed as flood-prone by the Rashtriya Barh Ayog?
accepted.x: The National Flood Commission assessed approximately 40 million hectares as flood-prone.
accepted.tq: Use order-of-magnitude discrimination for a high-risk quantitative fact.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The India Meteorological Department provides flash-flood guidance not only for India but also to which group of neighbouring countries?
accepted.x: IMD supplies flash-flood guidance for India and neighbouring Bangladesh, Bhutan and Nepal.
accepted.tq: Match the agency with the correct cross-border service recipients.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognised type of flood in the classification given?
accepted.x: Riverine, flash, coastal and urban floods are recognised types. ‘Tectonic flood’ is not included in this classification.
accepted.tq: Identify the odd term that describes an earthquake-related process rather than a flood type.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly classified as a structural flood-management measure?
accepted.x: Embankments and flood walls are structural measures. Flood forecasting, flood-plain zoning and flood insurance are non-structural measures.
accepted.tq: Separate physical engineering works from regulatory, informational and financial measures.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Flood insurance is a non-structural measure. Dams and reservoirs, and channel and drainage improvement are structural measures, while flood-plain zoning is non-structural.
accepted.tq: Find the classification reversal by comparing physical construction with policy and financial tools.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents a structural measure followed by a non-structural measure for flood management?
accepted.x: Sea walls are structural measures, whereas flood forecasting is non-structural. Detention basins and channel improvement are structural, while insurance, zoning and flood fighting are non-structural.
accepted.tq: Split each option into two parts and classify the first and second measures separately.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which environmental change accelerated surface runoff in upstream Nagaland during 2013–2023?
o: Expansion of glacial lakes in the Himalaya
Creation of 800 square kilometres of new forest
Clearing of about 800 square kilometres of forest
accepted.x: About 800 square kilometres of upstream Nagaland forest was cleared during 2013–2023, thereby increasing and accelerating runoff.
accepted.tq: Link the land-cover change with its hydrological consequence instead of treating the figure in isolation.
accepted.sec: Floods and flash floods - causes, riverine floods, GLOF, flood-prone area committees  [APPSC]
